# ECC: Genetic Tools — How to Optimize AI Agents for Software Engineering

The video features ECC, a set of open source tools to organize the work of code assistants with AI. Displays the components (subagents, skills, hooks and rules), the cycle of planning, testing, reviewing, remembering and improving, memory between sessions, security check with AgentShield and team plans.

Video by Maurício Yokoyama Issei, published on October 9, 2026 (8 min 37 s).
Watch: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o3IMxBLEhp0

_The video and the transcript are in Portuguese. The minutes between brackets, such as [04:12], point to the excerpt of the video._

## What is ECC

The video deals with ECC, which he presents as "Everything Claude Code": a complete framework that changes the way code assistants with AI work [00:00]. The video cites more than 1 million ECC skill installations in 30 days [00:21].

## In addition to basic prompts

When programming with AI, at first everything seems magical, but soon the AI forgets the context and ignores the process [01:03]. The video compares the unstructured AI to a brilliant but chaotic junior developer: fast, inconsistent and memoryless [01:25]. ECC flows function as a disciplined engineering manager: they bring structure, persistent memory and limits to keep the code safe [01:46].

ECC is not a configuration file: it functions as an operating system for the agent environment, with ready-made skills, planning, memory optimization and security [02:08]. The video cites more than 140,000 stars and 21,000 forks at GitHub, an award on Anthropic hackathon and documentation in more than 12 languages, including Portuguese [02:29].

## The components

The power of ECC comes from a modular ecosystem, not from a giant prompt [02:50]. The numbers below are those quoted in the video [03:10]:

- 68 specialized subagents, such as an architect or a security analyst, to delegate each task to the right profile [03:10];
- 293 skills, ready and reusable workflows [03:10];
- hooks, automations shooting alone during execution [03:10];
- mandatory rules, separated by programming language [03:31].

Together, rules, hooks and skills make the model follow the path, check the work itself and correct the code without having to ask [03:31].

Despite the name, ECC functions as a universal layer: in addition to Claude Code, it runs with Codex, Cursor, Gemini and OpenCode [04:13].

## The cycle of agentic engineering

The ECC makes the AI follow a five-step cycle [04:35]:

1. Plan architecture before writing code [04:35].
2. Test and implement in a flow of TDD [04:35].
3. Review and verify, with quality gates [04:56].
4. Remember decisions with unified memory [04:56].
5. Improve, extracting session patterns [04:56].

In the terminal, this becomes bar commands [04:56]. `/plan` calls the planner agent, `/tdd` calls the test guide, `/code-review` calls the quality subagent and `/build-fix` calls the build error solver [05:18].

## Memory and security

Unified memory attacks context amnesia: agents save what they have done, search the project history and keep the conversation between sessions [05:39]. If the chat window closes, nothing critical is lost [06:00].

With agents who have persistent access to the project, the question arises: what can they access [06:00]? AgentShield checks configuration security [06:21]. According to the video, it runs 102 static analysis rules and more than 1,200 tests [06:21]. It reads prompts and settings and ensures that secrets, such as API keys, are not exposed [06:42].

## For teams

The video describes three levels [07:02]:

- the free open source layer for those who work alone and run local flows [07:02];
- the GitHub App or Pro plans for private repositories and teams, at US$ 19 per seat per month [07:02];
- the Enterprise plan, tailored, with dedicated deployment and training [07:24].

The video quotes an Amazon engineering leader: an engineer thought a team of 10 to 15 people was working on what one person did with the tools [07:24].

## Final reflection

The final question: Does today’s AI configuration look like a chaotic junior, who needs supervision all the time, or a predictable and disciplined engineering team [08:05]?

## Frequently Asked Questions

### The ECC only works with Claude Code?

Nope. According to the video, it also runs with Codex, Cursor, Gemini and OpenCode [04:13].

### What cycle does the ECC impose?

Plan, test and implement, review, remember and improve [04:35].

### What is Agent Shield?

It is the ECC security check: audit the configuration and ensure that secrets such as API keys are not exposed [06:21].

## About the video

In this video, we explore the **ECC (Everything Claude Code)**, the operational layer and open source toolkit created by **Affaan Mustafa (`affaan-m`)** to optimize the performance of AI encoding agents.

Learn how ECC transforms AI assistants — how **Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode** — in a disciplined software engineering system. We approach the architecture of **specialised subagents**, **Reusable skills**, **automation by hooks**, **persistent memory** and safety audits with **Agentshield**.
